lawyer:
Md Abdul Kader Bhuiyan, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Natai Roy Chowdhury with Mithun Roy Chowdhury, Advocates ----- For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Mosaraf Hossain Dhali and others ------- Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners
Vs
 Khalilur Rahman Bepari and others ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1(ka) 12 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006 and 7-9-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 170 of 2002 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those of dated 6-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 101 of 2001 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 101 of 2001 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur against the defendant-respondent-petitioners and others for a declaration of title with a further declaration that the deed in the name of the defendants No. 29-32 is collusive, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs along with a prayer for recovery of khash possession contending inter alia, that the suit properties appertaining to Mouza Ichli under Chandpur Sadar comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land out of 6.97 acres of land originally belonged to one Loknath and others. Subsequently, one Nurul Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and a Sekander Sheikh in 04 annas share obtained settlement from the original owners Loknath and others. During CS operation the suit land went under water and after its appearance from the bad of the river the Ex-Zaminder filed a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 in which the settlement holders Nurul Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham. Thereafter, while Nurul Islam and Sekandar failed to pay the rent the Ex-Zamindar started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and in .Rent Execution Case No. 02 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain. Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land by way of 'boynama' on 10-3-1951. The further case of the present petitioners i.e. the plaintiffs is such that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Mohammad Ali and others by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 21-12-1956 became the owner of the suit land. The auction purchaser Zamir Hossain exhausted his share after his transfer. Thereafter, the SA khatian No. 28 was correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land measuring 3.60 acres. The father of the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the land-in-dispute and after his demise the land was inherited by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs after erecting their homestead in the suit properties use to possess the same and also paying rent to the government regularly. Out of the total land 42 decimals was recorded in the name of the plaintiff during BS operation and 461/2 decimals went into the khash khatian of the government. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit land is in the khash land of the government but taking advantage of that the defendants No. 29-32 and 33-36 collusively obtained settlement from the government by kabuliyat dated 22-5-2000. On 20-2-2001 all on a sudden the defendants No. 29-32 dispossessed the plaintiffs from the 'kW schedule land forcibly and erected huts therein. The plaintiffs to the suit thereafter learnt about the settlement of the defendants from the government and after getting certified copy of the kabuliyate on 11-6-2001 filed the original suit.

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No. 2-32 and 33-36 after filing separate written statements contended that the land measuring 84.00 acres under Mouza Ichuli of SA plot No. 251 is the khash land of the government and BS khatian has been correctly prepared in the name of the government in its khash kahtian No. 1. The defendants being landless persons prayed for settlement of the land from the government and the government being satisfied by way of registered kabuliyat No. 2481 and 2485 granted settlement in favour of the defendants on 22-5-2000. The further case of the contesting defendants is such the plaintiff No. 4 admitting the title of the government in its khash khatian No. 1 took settlement of 25 decimals of land in Settlement Case No. 178/199-2000. The plaintiff No. 4after taking settlement from the government erecting homestead use to possess the same. It is the case of the defendants that the plaintiffs were never dispossessed from the suit properties since they had no possession therein but only to grab the government property on the basis of false allegations and created forged papers filed the original suit.

4. The leaned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 6-10-2002.

5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred a Title Suit being No. 170 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chandpur which was transmitted to the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Chandpur for hearing and disposal. The learned appellate court hearing the appeal allowed 'the same by the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil. Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay.

7. During hearing of this Rule Mr Md Abdul Kader Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury and Mr Mithun Roy Chowdhury the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite-parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal committed illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment of reversal in the eye of law as the learned lower appellate court violating the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure decided the merit of the appeal arbitrarily in favour of the plaintiffs without reversing the findings and decisions of the trial court adverting evidence therein. The learned Advocate also submits that there has been non-reading and misreading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and the impugned judgment and decree was passed by the Appellate Court in a slipshod manner and not applying it's judicial mind. The learned Advocate submits that the Appellate Court not assessed the evidence on records in its true perspective and evaluated the same causing miscarriage of justice. The learned court during taking decision not at all considered all the papers on records properly and the plaintiffs to the suit during trial utterly failed to discharge their onus in proving their respective case. But the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur without taking it into consideration decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and in fact there is no paper showing the existence of the Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Nur Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham as alleged comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the impugned judgment and decree is highly defective and it is not at all enforceable as it is not a speaking decree. The plaintiffs' original suit was a suit not for declaration of title, but for a declaration that the kabuliyat in favour of the defendants in respect of settlement is collusive, forged and not acted upon along with further prayer of recovery of khash possession. The learned Appellate Court misconceived the matter from the very beginning and, as such, failed to consider that the plaintiffs were totally failed to prove their possession and dispossession in the disputed property by producing tangible evidence. The learned Advocate submits that the learned Lower Appellate Court also failed to appreciate that, among the plaintiffs the plaintiffs No. 4 and 5 admitting the right, title, interest of the government in the suit property took settlement from the government and the conclusive findings with regard to this from the side of the trial court was not reversed by the appellate court adverting evidence on records. The learned Advocate relying upon the provisions laid down in section 115 of the Evidence Act argued that the plaintiffs are stopped from challenging the title of the Government inasmuch as among them some of the plaintiffs admitting the title of the government in its khash khatian No. 1 obtained settlement by kabuliyate.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to the suit during trial after adducing sufficient evidence proved their case that the original owners of the disputed properties were Loknath and others and from them one Nurul Islam Sheikh and Sekandar Sheikh in 12 annas and 04 annas share took settlement. The learned Advocate also submits that during CS operation although the land-in-dispute went under water but subsequently it was re-appeared by alleviation and the Ex-Zamindar pursuant to a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 gave the land amicably in favour of their settlement holders Nur Islam and Sekandar Sk. and in fact the partition suit was ended in favour of the Plaintiff's-Predecessors Nur Islam and Sekandar. Subsequently, for arrear of rent a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 was started and in Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land on 10-3-1951 and from that Zamir Hossain; predecessors of the plaintiffs kabala purchased the land-in-dispute. The learned Advocate also submits that the Lower Appellate Court during deciding the merit of the appeal after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below.

10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates I have perused the case records, pleadings of the respective parties, impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in consultation with the judgment and dismissal decree passed by the trial court, evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties and all other connected papers on records.

11. On perusal of the case records; it transpires that the positive contention as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs was such that the land-in-dispute originally belonged to ex-Zamindars namely Loknath and others. From them one Nur Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and one Sekandar Sheikh in 04 annas share took settlement. It is an admitted position that during CS operation the land in dispute went under water of the river. With regard to this; it is the contention of the plaintiffs that while the land-in-dispute reappeared from the bad of the river the ex-Zamindar started a "Touzi Bontan" (Partition Suit) Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and in that suit the settlement holder Nur Islam and Sekandar Sheikh obtained their respective saham in respect of the suit properties. The further pleadings of the plaintiffs were such that the Zaminders for arrears of rent started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and obtained a decree. In decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the land by way of "Boynama" on 10-3-1951. From that auction purchaser the predecessors of the plaintiffs obtained the suit land.

12. Vis-a-vis; it is the plain case of the contesting defendants that they are the landless cultivators and inasmuch as the property-in-dispute is the khash land of the government they prayed for settlement and the government being satisfied on 22-5-2000 by two registered kabuliyats No. 2481 and 2485 granted settlement in favour of the contesting defendants. It was further contended from the side of the defendants in their pleadings that the plaintiffs had no manner of title, possession and interest in the disputed properties and thereby there is no question of dispossession from the side of the defendants as alleged from the side of the Plaintiff-Opposite parties.

13. In this context; having gone through the case records I find that the plaintiffs to the suit to substantiate their claim examined 5 (five) witnesses and on the contrary the defendants examined 3 (three) witnesses.

14. PW 1 is the plaintiff No. 5 himself namely Abdul Hamid Bepari. This witness in his examination-in-chief frankly conceded at a stage that during the CS operation the land-in dispute went under water and subsequently when the land reappeared the ex-Zamindar started a Partition Suit in which the earlier settlement holders of the Zaminders namely Nur Islam and Sekander Sheikh obtained a separate saham in respect of the suit properties. The plaintiff No. 5 in his testimony testified at a stage that during BS operation the land measuring 461/2 decimals become the khash land of the government in its khash khatian No.1. In his cross-examination he testified at a stage that they did not submit any paper showing the existence of the Partition Suit No. 65 of 1930 and also did not produce the judgment and decree passed in Rent Suit No. 350 of 1950. The plaintiff also admitted that they could not furnish any paper showing the existence of decree of the Execution case. At a stage of his testimony P.W.1 testifies that they did not sought for any relief against the government with regard to SA khatian which stands recorded in the name of government. He expressed his inability to state the CS khatian of the disputed property and also expressed his inability to state about the area of land in CS plot No. 251.

15. It is to be noted here that the learned trial court in his observation and findings pointed out specifically about the discrimination and contradictions with material omissions as transpired within the depositions of the plaintiff's witnesses. The plaintiff No. 5 in his testimony testifies categorically at a stage-(quote):

“নালিশা ভূমি (২৫১ দাগের) সরকার হতে কারা বন্দোবস্ত প্রাপ্ত হয়েছে তা জানি না। তাদেরকে অত্র মামলায় পক্ষ করিনি। নালিশা ভূমিতে যে আশ্রয়ন প্রকল্প আছে তাতে প্রায় ৩০০/৪০০ জন লোক বসবাস করেন। তন্মেধ্যে আমি এ মামলায় কাউকেই পক্ষ করিনি। বাদীরা সবাই আমার ভাই বোন। ৪নং বাদী আবুল হোসেন বেপারী ১৭৮/৯৯-২০০০নং বন্দোবস্ত মামলা মূলে নালিশা ২৫১ দাগের খাস ২৫ শতক বাবদ বন্দোবস্ত পেলে তার নামে ৫৪১ নং জোত খতিয়ান খোলার বিষয় আমার জানা নাই। আমরা সবাই নালিশা ভূমিতে বসবাস করি না।

16. In another stage of his deposition he (PW 1) deposed that they did not submit the papers of Mutation Case No. 40 of 2000-2001 and also not impleaded the government as a party to their suit in the name of whom 84 acres of land has been recorded as khash khatian.

17. The witness number two of the plaintiffs PW 2 Oli Miah Bepari in his testimony testifies at a stage that the plaintiffs possessed the land for about 40/45 years and the defendants Bachchu and Mosharraf Dhali dispossessed the plaintiffs from 53 decimals of land. In the cross-examination this witness testified that the plaintiffs are his (PW 2) paternal brothers and sisters.

18. The other possession witness of the plaintiffs PW 3 Ruhul Amin Bepari who happens to be another relative of the plaintiffs testifies at a stage that he cannot say about the original owners of the suit property from whom the plaintiffs acquired the suit land.

19. PW 4 Ashraf Ali Gazi is one of the vendors of the plaintiff's predecessor who transferred 06 decimals of land by a sub-kabala dated 27-6-1980.

20. The last witness of the plaintiffs is the attesting witness of a deed dated 17-2-1987 which has been marked as Exhibit-5(ka).

21. On the other hand the witness No. 1 of the defendants Md Amir Hossain is a Tahsilder, who deposed on behalf of the government and corroborated the case of the defendants. This witness testified about the settlement khatian in favour of the defendants by way of kabuliyats being No. 2481 and 2485. He also submitted the papers relating to the right, title, and interest of the government with regard to khash khatian No. 1 and the settlement khatian in favour of the plaintiff No. 4 and all these papers has been duly exhibited.

22. The defendant No. 29 Mosharrof Hossain as DW 2 testified before the learned trial court and deposed in support of their pleadings.

23. The last witness of the defendants Md Mojibor Rahman Sheikh corroborated the case of the contesting defendants No. 29-32. It was contended by the witness No. 3 in his deposition that there exist "গুচ্ছ গ্রাম" in the said properties wherein the settlement holders of the government use to possess and do reside in their homesteads.

24. On meticulous consideration and assessment of evidence it is evident to note that the witnesses produced from the side of the plaintiffs has become shaky and contradicted one-another in respect of material aspects. Furthermore; they are not independent disinterested and credible witnesses who can be relied upon to substantiate or prove the case of the plaintiffs; but on the other hand, the witness Nos. 1, 2 and 3 of the defendants despite were thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the plaintiffs but none of them appears to have been discredited.

<u>25. it is a decided matter that under the ambit of sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act it is the incumbent duty upon the plaintiffs to the suit to discharge their onus of proof in proving their respective case but in the instant case as I have come across from the evidence on records that the plaintiffs to the suit could not discharge their onus of proof as observed by the learned trial Judge in his judgment and dismissal decree. The learned lower appellate court at the time of passing the impugned judgment and decree without reversing the conclusive findings of the trial court on the title, possession and dispossession as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs reversed the judgment and decree as a whole which is a clear violation of the provision laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Under this provision of law in case of reversal of the trial court's judgment the Appellate Court is under legal obligation in reversing the findings of the trial court and give bona fide reasons for it's decision on the points for determination and shall have to give reasons therein at its own independent findings. The appellate court must contain definite findings on the question involved and must give reason when reversing the material findings of the trial court [Ref: Mohsena vs Habib, 17 BLD (AD) 47, Abu vs Sharifa, 15 BLD (AD) 91, Nur vs Nur 40 DLR (AD) 175, Abdus vs Jonab (Md) 57 DLR (AD) 112, Profulla vs Nagen, 6 BLC (AD) 1301.</u>

26. Having regard to the aforesaid legal proposition I have the reason to inclined such a view that the arguments advanced from the side of the learned counsel Mr Abdul Kader Bhuiyan having much nexus are acceptable in view of the judgment and decree passed by the Lower Appellate Court. The impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal in the eye of law inasmuch as the legal lacuna which is already transpired within the case of the plaintiffs has been totally overlooked as well as ignored from the side of the Lower Appellate Court and ignoring the material facts and evidence of the case the impugned judgment and decree was passed which is not sustainable in the eye of law.

27. Besides this; the chain of title since not at all proved from the side of the plaintiffs which is badly required and the possession and dispossession as alleged from their side as not proved by tangible evidence the plaintiffs are not entitled the relief as prayed for.

28. In the forgoing narrative; having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule have got much merit to succeed.

29. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006 and 7-9-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 170 of 2002 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those of dated 6-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 101 of 2001 is hereby set aside.

30. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

Communicate the judgment and order immediately and send back the lower Court's record at once.

End.
